### PQB_MSQ_M1: Identify all cell types present in loose connective tissue matrix: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Fibroblasts
- [ ] B) Mast cells
- [ ] C) Histocytes
- [ ] D) Osteons
- [ ] E) Plasma cells

> **✅ Answers:** A) Fibroblasts, B) Mast cells, C) Histocytes, E) Plasma cells
> **Explanation:** Areolar CT contains fibroblasts, mast cells, histocytes, plasma cells.

- [ ] A) Neutrophils
- [ ] B) Eosinophils
- [ ] C) Basophils
- [ ] D) Monocytes

### PQB_MSQ_M3: From a Question Bank perspective, select all locations featuring Pseudostratified Ciliated Columnar Epithelium: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Trachea lumen
- [ ] B) Large bronchi branches
- [ ] C) Nasopharynx passage
- [ ] D) Fallopian tube mucosa

### PQB_MSQ_M4: From a Question Bank perspective, select all connective tissue sheaths organizing skeletal muscle blocks: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] B) Perimysium surrounding muscle fascicles
- [ ] C) Epimysium surrounding whole muscle belly
- [ ] D) Perichondrium
- [ ] E) Periosteum

> **✅ Answers:** A) Endomysium surrounding individual fibers, B) Perimysium surrounding muscle fascicles, C) Epimysium surrounding whole muscle belly
> **Explanation:** Muscle sheaths = Endomysium, Perimysium, Epimysium.

### PQB_MSQ_M5: In Question Bank Medium deck, select all sensory organs containing Bipolar Neurones: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] B) Olfactory epithelium of nose
- [ ] C) Vestibulocochlear organ of inner ear

### PQB_MSQ_M6: In Question Bank Medium deck, select all characteristics of Dense Regular Connective Tissue: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Compact parallel white collagen fiber bundles
- [ ] B) Fibroblasts arranged in rows between collagen strands
- [ ] C) High tensile strength along direction of fiber orientation
- [ ] D) Forms Tendons connecting muscle to bone
- [ ] E) Random meshwork of fibers resisting multidirectional stress

> **✅ Answers:** A) Compact parallel white collagen fiber bundles, B) Fibroblasts arranged in rows between collagen strands, C) High tensile strength along direction of fiber orientation, D) Forms Tendons connecting muscle to bone
> **Explanation:** Dense regular CT contains parallel collagen bundles and row-arranged fibroblasts in tendons.

### PQB_MSQ_M7: In Question Bank Medium deck, select all true statements regarding Bone vs Cartilage matrix: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Bone matrix is hard and mineralized with Ossein and Calcium Phosphate
- [ ] B) Cartilage matrix is solid pliable chondrin with anti-angiogenic factors
- [ ] C) Bone possesses Haversian canals and rich blood supply
- [ ] D) Cartilage is avascular and nourished by perichondrial diffusion
- [ ] E) Both bone and cartilage matrix contain mineralized calcium hydroxyapatite

> **✅ Answers:** A) Bone matrix is hard and mineralized with Ossein and Calcium Phosphate, B) Cartilage matrix is solid pliable chondrin with anti-angiogenic factors, C) Bone possesses Haversian canals and rich blood supply, D) Cartilage is avascular and nourished by perichondrial diffusion
> **Explanation:** Bone has mineralized ossein and Haversian canals; cartilage has pliable avascular chondrin.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="In Question Bank Medium deck, select all" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>

### PQB_MSQ_M8: In Question Bank Medium deck, select all features of Transitional Epithelium (Urothelium): (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Multilayered compound plastic epithelium
- [ ] B) Surface pear-shaped or umbrella cells
- [ ] C) High distensibility and stretch capacity
- [ ] D) Lines urinary bladder, ureters, and renal pelvis
- [ ] E) Keratinized protective dead stratum corneum

> **✅ Answers:** A) Multilayered compound plastic epithelium, B) Surface pear-shaped or umbrella cells, C) High distensibility and stretch capacity, D) Lines urinary bladder, ureters, and renal pelvis
> **Explanation:** Urothelium is a distensible compound epithelium with umbrella cells lining urinary tract.

### PQB_MSQ_M9: In Question Bank Medium deck, select all true statements regarding Blood Clotting mechanism: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Injured tissues release Thromboplastin
- [ ] B) Calcium ions (Ca2+) are required for prothrombin activator formation
- [ ] C) Active Thrombin converts soluble Fibrinogen into insoluble Fibrin
- [ ] D) Blood platelets aggregate to form primary platelet plug
- [ ] E) Heparin acts as essential enzyme converting fibrinogen to fibrin

> **✅ Answers:** A) Injured tissues release Thromboplastin, B) Calcium ions (Ca2+) are required for prothrombin activator formation, C) Active Thrombin converts soluble Fibrinogen into insoluble Fibrin, D) Blood platelets aggregate to form primary platelet plug
> **Explanation:** Clotting involves thromboplastin release, Ca2+, thrombin conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin, and platelet aggregation.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="In Question Bank Medium deck, select all" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>

### PQB_MSQ_M10: In Question Bank Medium deck, select all neuroglial cells present in Peripheral Nervous System (PNS): (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Myelinating Schwann cells
- [ ] B) Ganglionic Satellite cells
- [ ] C) CNS Astrocytes
- [ ] D) CNS Microglia
- [ ] E) CNS Oligodendrocytes
